title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
summary: Hold: the indirect-cost-only rating conflicts with the documented licensing and billing routes the briefing itself describes. Copilot agent access can incur Copilot Credits consumption, and the proposed management APIs require an Agent 365 licence; unpublished A2A-specific charges do not remove those requirements.

claims.claim: Whether calling the installed Agent 365 A2A agent itself consumes Copilot Credits is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent2Agent A2A connected agent licensing billing Copilot Credits additional charge. Read prerequisites and connected-agent pages. Copilot Studio A2A results describe a different harness/connector mechanism, not the Agent 365 registration mechanism.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cost is low, meaning indirect cost only, and the only cost the sources show is admin time.
claims.quote: The only cost the sources show is admin time; ... Microsoft documents Copilot agent access through Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and Copilot Chat usage-based billing. ... Package Management API access requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.fix: Set cost to variable. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Variable. Copilot agent access can use pay-as-you-go billing measured in Copilot Credits, and Package Management API access requires an Agent 365 licence. A2A-specific additional charges are not yet published.' Remove 'Treat the cost known today as admin time and communications.' Retain the narrower uncertainty about whether the A2A call itself consumes credits; do not describe that call as proven metered.
